item.title: Safe and Trustworthy Autonomous Systems in Real-World Environments
item.content:encoded:
Heye Huang, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

Inhi Kim, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

Boqi Li, Beihang University

Haotian Shi, Tongji University

Lei Yang, Nanyang Technological University

Kailai Sun, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

Autonomous systems operating in complex real-world environments face significant challenges in ensuring safety, reliability, and generalization. This special issue seeks research that advances trustworthy autonomy through integration of data-driven learning with structured knowledge, world models, formal verification, and uncertainty reasoning. Contributions should address both average-case and long-tail safety-critical scenarios, with emphasis on how autonomous systems can identify risks, adapt continually, and coordinate with other agents.

The scope includes autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, and other safety-critical platforms. Submissions may combine learning, optimization, control, simulation, and human-centered methods provided they clearly contribute to trustworthy autonomous behavior. The issue welcomes original research, reviews, benchmarks, and perspective articles demonstrating methodological novelty, rigorous evaluation, or insights transferable to real-world autonomous system deployment.

Appel publié par Expert Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Trustworthy autonomy and safety principles
  • Uncertainty modeling and robustness
  • Runtime assurance for learning-enabled systems
  • Navigation and manipulation robotics
  • Mobile robotics and spatial intelligence
  • Perception-action learning
  • Active exploration and embodied decision-making
  • LLM/VLM-enabled autonomy
  • Agentic AI and multimodal perception
  • Tool-using agents and knowledge-enhanced models
  • Foundation model adaptation for physical systems
  • Risk representation and uncertainty-aware perception
  • Behavior prediction and occupancy modeling
  • Scene modeling and world models
  • Safety-critical interaction anticipation
  • Episodic and semantic memory
  • Experience retrieval and in-context adaptation
  • Continual learning and self-evolving autonomy
  • Recursive self-improvement under safety constraints
  • Safe adaptation in changing environments
  • Risk-aware planning and constrained optimization
  • Safe reinforcement learning
  • Decision making under uncertainty
  • Model-predictive control approaches
  • Closed-loop safety mechanisms
  • Rare-event discovery and scenario generation
  • Generative simulation and counterfactual testing
  • Adversarial and stress testing
  • Digital twins and safety assessment
  • Connected and automated vehicles
  • V2X-enabled cooperation
  • Multi-agent coordination
  • Traffic-level autonomy and infrastructure intelligence
  • System-wide mobility optimization

Timeline

  • May 1, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Multimodal Learning for Embodied Intelligence: Perception, Alignment, Fusion, Reasoning, and Generation
item.content:encoded:
Zhiliang Wu, Nanyang Technological University

Kun Li, United Arab Emirates University

Yunqiu Xu, National University of Singapore

Embodied intelligence systems must integrate diverse sensory inputs—vision, language, audio, touch, 3D signals, and action trajectories—to perceive and act in the physical world. This special issue focuses on multimodal learning approaches that enable embodied agents to build effective world models from these heterogeneous inputs. The work addresses unique challenges in embodied settings, including spatiotemporal understanding, cross-modal fusion, causal reasoning, and handling real-world conditions like noise, missing data, and partial observability.

The special issue invites research on multimodal representation learning, information fusion, and reasoning methods for embodied systems. Studies should explore how embodied agents leverage foundation models and integrate multiple modalities for tasks ranging from perception and interaction to planning, decision-making, and world model generation.

Appel publié par Expert Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Multimodal Representation Learning for Embodied World Models
  • Multimodal Fusion for Embodied Perception and Interaction
  • Multimodal Reasoning for Planning and Decision-Making
  • Multimodal Generating for Embodied World
  • Vision-Language-Action Modeling
  • Spatial-Temporal and 3D/4D Scene Understanding
  • Predictive and Memory-Augmented World Models
  • Foundation Models for Embodied Systems
  • Trustworthy Embodied Multimodal Learning and Applications

Timeline

  • March 31, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Robotics in Advertising and Marketing
item.content:encoded:
Mark Yi-Cheon Yim, University of Massachusetts Lowell

Esther Kang, University of Bristol

The rapidly evolving landscape of home robotics presents new opportunities for advertising and marketing. With advances in physical AI making robots more capable of interacting in everyday environments, and demographic shifts creating increased demand for in-home robotics, major technology companies are now commercializing robots for caregiving and other household functions. These robots offer a novel channel for brand engagement, as human-robot interactions can foster emotional connections that position robots as both companions and marketing agents.

This special issue seeks high-quality research examining the intersection of robotics, marketing, and advertising. The journal invites contributions exploring how consumers engage with robotic agents, how these interactions affect brand perception and consumer behavior, and how marketing strategies can effectively leverage robotic technologies. Research employing diverse methodologies and addressing topics ranging from human-robot interaction psychology to ethical and privacy considerations is welcome.

Appel publié par Journal of Interactive Advertising. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Human–Robot Interaction: Psychological effects of perceived vitality, animacy, and agency in brand-representative robots
  • Social and Relational Marketing: Use of social robots to build brand loyalty, foster parasocial relationships, and address consumer isolation through interactive engagement
  • Care Robotics: Roles of interactive robots in home and specialized contexts, including navigation, product recommendation, and customer service
  • Technology Adoption: Factors and mechanisms that influence consumer adoption of robots in domestic settings
  • Experiential and Event Marketing: Effectiveness of robotic installations in creating immersive brand experiences and interactive out-of-home (OOH) advertising
  • Ethical and Privacy Considerations: Issues of consumer trust, data privacy, and the ethical implications of autonomous data collection by robotic agents in advertising and marketing contexts
  • Measurement and Metrics: Development of frameworks for assessing ROI and consumer engagement in human–robot interactive advertising campaigns

Timeline

  • October 10, 2027: Manuscript deadline
